chunks: “Indeed, al-Shaytan comes to a man from among our followers at the time of his death, from his right and from his left, to lead him astray from what he is upon. But Allah, Mighty and Majestic, refuses that. And that is the saying of Allah, Exalted is He:
“Allah keeps firm those who believe with the firm word in the life of this world and in the Hereafter.”

key_terms.أَوْلِيَائِنَا: our followers or devoted adherents, referring to the people loyal to the Ahl al-Bayt عليهم السلام
key_terms.الشَّيْطَانَ: Shaytan, who seeks to mislead the believer at the time of death
key_terms.الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا: those who believe, the faithful recipients of divine firmness
key_terms.الْآخِرَةِ: the Hereafter, where the effect of this firmness also continues
key_terms.بِالْقَوْلِ الثَّابِتِ: with the firm word, meaning steadfast affirmation of true faith
key_terms.لِيُضِلَّهُ: to lead him astray from the truth and faith he held
key_terms.مَوْتِهِ: his death, the moment when this trial and divine firmness are manifested
key_terms.يُثَبِّتُ: He makes firm, meaning Allah grants steadfastness

ai.seo_question: How does Allah keep believers firm at the time of death according to Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith states that at the moment of death, al-Shaytan attempts to misguide the believers from the truth they held in life. Allah, however, grants firmness to the faithful, and the Imam عليه السلام cites the Qur'anic verse as proof of this divine support in both this world and the Hereafter.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.360 - Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as) said:

"Indeed, Shaytan comes to one of our followers at the time of their death, approaching from their right and from their left to lead them astray from what they are upon. But Allah (swt), the Mighty and Glorious, refuses this, and this is the meaning of Allah’s (swt) words:
'Allah (swt) will keep firm those who believe, with the firm word, in this worldly life and in the Hereafter'" (Surah Ibrahim 14:27).
